calibration_notes.jbook_corpus_coverage: The pentagon_jbook corpus (verticals/public_co/data/_jbook_data/programs.json) is auto-seeded from FY2026 PB exhibits and case-study extractions (initial seeds: YSS/Wolfpack 2026-05-11, IonQ/Wolfpack 2026-02-04). It carries 410 PE shells but only a subset have FY-by-FY funding rows populated. For a 2023-01-15 PIT cutoff, the great majority of Boeing-relevant PEs return NOT_FOUND_IN_TIMERANGE because FY2023 rows have not been hand-extracted yet. This is a corpus-extension gap, NOT a J-Book divergence pattern.
calibration_notes.false_positive_protection: The F-15 / F01500 procurement line returned UNFUNDED_TWO_PLUS_YEARS with only FY2008=$0 and FY2023=$0 history — clearly a sparse-row artifact (real F-15EX procurement was funded throughout this period). Heuristic #7 + skepticism about sparse history rows is what kept this from being a false-positive RED_FLAG.
calibration_notes.what_a_real_test_would_need: For the J-BOOK EXPOSURE DIVERGENCE PATTERN to fire on BA at this PIT, the corpus would need FY2022-FY2025 PB exhibit rows for KC-46A (0401221F), F-15EX (0207146F), V-22 (0401318F), B-52 (0101113F), and F/A-18E/F PE. The framework piping is correct (queries fire, signals map per rubric); the bottleneck is corpus extraction depth, which the cohort-extension guide explicitly anticipates.
